_doc: Owned by AI-A. Per regular: beats[i] fires on that owner's (i+1)th successful handover. line is spoken via passenger_said; every beat also toasts. Beats are hints/flavour about the Zero Line.

own_001.line: Hands are black as ever, but I can hold a shovel again. Cheers.
Third time you've found my things. Maybe you're the lucky one.
The engine room hums when the Zero Line is near a station. Never seen the front of this train, mind.
Come by the engine room sometime. The tea's always hot. The coal never runs out, funny that.
I shovel less each winter. The engine feels lighter, and I swear it's your doing. Don't stop.

own_002.line: You're a marvel, darling. I shall mention you in my memoirs.
I met a conductor once who swore this train has no last stop. I laughed. I no longer laugh.
A lady in the dining car sang a song nobody knew, and everyone cried. Strange, no?
For you, darling: the Zero Line forgives those who keep looking.
Darling, I've worked it out. We are all lost property, and the Zero Line is merely the shelf. Do mind who collects us.

own_003.line: Hooray! Mum says I shouldn't talk to strangers but you're not a stranger, you're the Lost Property man!
I counted the carriages. Six! Then I counted again and there were still six, but different.
Pip's secret: the lamp in your car gets brighter when you're kind. I tested it.
I'm going to be a Lost Property attendant when I grow up. Can I have your hat?
I walked to the very front. There's a little door with a tag on it. The tag says 'unclaimed'. I didn't open it. Mum says that's other people's.

own_004.line: Elementary, as I said. Though I confess, I'd never have found it myself.
A curious pattern: nothing is ever truly lost on this train. Only misplaced in time.
I have been mapping the stops. They repeat, yet no two are alike. Fascinating.
Your methods are sound, attendant. Should the Zero Line ever need a detective, I know whom to recommend.
Every lost thing has an owner somewhere, attendant. Find the owner of the Zero Line and I suspect you've found its last stop.

own_005.line: Right on time. You and I would get along on any route.
Schedules on this line are written in pencil. The stops erase and redraw themselves.
I carried a parcel once for a man who never got off. It's still in the Luggage car, I think.
Next stop, friend: wherever you want. That's what the Zero Line is for.
The parcel in the Luggage car has a new label overnight, in my handwriting. Some things aren't delivered until you're ready to take them.

own_006.line: Have a biscuit, dear. Go on, I made them myself, in the Sleeper car.
I've been on this train longer than I can say. It's a kind place, if you let it be.
I've started knitting you a scarf. Don't tell. It's the colour of lamplight.
The scarf is finished. Wear it when the night gets long.
I boarded to visit someone. I forget who. I stayed to keep the kettle on. That's a sort of arriving, I think.

own_007.line: I could write a sonnet about this. In fact, I just did. It rhymes poorly. I'm thrilled.
The rhythm of the wheels gives me my best lines. Four beats, then a rest, forever.
I wrote a poem for the lost things. It begins with a station, and ends with you.
Poets say every train has one last stop. I rather think ours is a very long comma.
Every ending I write, the train politely declines. It wants a better one. One where somebody says 'that's mine.'

own_008.line: Abracadabra, and there it is! Your cut of the applause, attendant.
A good trick is never explained. But I'll tell you: this train does all my best ones for free.
I tried to make the Zero Line disappear once. It just kept going. Rude.
The only real magic is returning something someone thought was gone for good. You do it every night.
Final trick: I tried to put the whole train in a hat. Wouldn't fit. Too heavy with everyone's maybes.

own_009.line: How terribly kind. I shall remember this, always.
I used to ride first class on the grand lines. Here, nobody asks my name, and I find I like it.
You've done me the loveliest service. Allow me one confidence: the Zero Line only stops for people who are still looking for something.
Should you ever tire of this car, attendant, the Observation car has a seat with your name on it.
I confess, dear, I'm still looking. I rather hope I never find it. The train, being polite, keeps stopping for me.

own_010.line: Delivered! Well, returned. Same thing, practically.
I carry letters between stops. Some are addressed to people who got off years ago. I deliver them anyway.
One letter was addressed to you, you know. I'm not allowed to say what it said. It said 'thank you'.
The Zero Line delivers everything eventually. Even you, perhaps, to wherever you're going.
I found the one letter I could never deliver. The address is just 'The Zero Line'. No sender, either.

own_011.line: Now I can see my way home. Thank you.
I light lamps along the corridor each night. Someone has to keep the dark honest.
I saw a light at the very front of the train, once. Steady and warm. I think it's waiting.
Keep your lamp lit, attendant. The brightest ones can be seen from the last stop.
I opened the little door at the front. A lantern on a hook, with a blank ticket tied to it. That's the light I saw. It's still waiting.

own_012.line: Fascinating! And yet, here it is. The data supports you.
I've been measuring the length of this train. It varies with the passengers' memories. Remarkable.
Hypothesis: the Zero Line is the sum of everything people couldn't let go. Your job is the most important job aboard.
Peer review complete. Your methods are sound. Keep examining, attendant.
New data: the train's interior gains a carriage-length for each unclaimed item, and loses one for each returned. You are, statistically, shortening the line.

own_013.line: Thank you thank you thank you! I'll never ever lose it again. Probably.
I went all the way to the Dining car by myself! The cook gave me a spoon of jam!
I found a coin under my seat but I put it in the Lost Property box. Was that right?
When I'm big I'm going to find lost things too. You're the best.
I looked for my name in the Lost Property book and it wasn't there. So I'm not lost! I'm just on a long ride.

own_014.line: Music to my ears. Ha. Thank you, friend.
I used to hear this train in my sleep as a boy. Same song, every night. Never knew why.
The wheels play a tune if you listen just so. I've been trying to write it down for forty years.
I've finally got it, the Zero Line's song. Here, hum along. Shh. Listen.
The Zero Line's song has a last note. The wheels always stop just short of it. I think it's waiting for someone to hum it.

own_015.line: The stars sent you. Thank you.
The stars here are different. They're stops, I think. Tiny, far-off stations we haven't reached yet.
I charted our course. It's a circle that never closes. And yet we're always getting somewhere.
Between us: the last stop is whichever one you're ready to get off at.
I redrew the chart. Every stop points at the Lost Property car. The last stop may not be on the map at all, only in a handing-over.
